title: AI is already in your pocket.
subtitle: It is just only ever in one pocket at a time.

title: Your AI and your colleague's have never met.
bullets: Two people, two phones, two separate assistants.
You screenshot one and paste it into the other.
Whatever you agreed never reaches either of them.
illustration: Two phones side by side, each with its own AI chat, and a screenshot being forwarded from one to the other. Buildable without a shoot.

title: Put everyone's pocket in the same room.
bullets: One conversation, shared across everybody's phone.
In the messaging app they already have open.
An agent in the middle, sorting out who wants what.
illustration: THE money shot. The 4-up frame mid-conflict: Julie's phone, Tom's phone, the room view showing the agent's “Tom's villa is 16k, Julie's cap is 12k”, and the artifact.

title: Text a bot. You are in.
bullets: No app to download. No account to create. No login to share.
Send someone the code and their phone is in the room too.
An agent joins exactly the same way a person does.
illustration: One phone: “new” → the room code and QR come straight back. A second phone joins. Two real screens.

title: One orchestrator. N humans. N agents.
highlight: Only the orchestrator sees every thread — which is how it can tell you that what you just asked for contradicts what someone else asked for.

caption: The sandbox is the isolation boundary: nobody's laptop, and no member's credentials inside it. The room reaches the agent through the daemon; the agent reaches back out through one MCP tool, and only that one.

title: One room, in everyone's pocket.
subtitle: You are not the middleman anymore.

title: On a real phone, not a mock.
bullets: Texted “new” from a phone — a working room, with a shared document, in 86 seconds.
Two people on two surfaces: every message attributed, one answer reaching both.
Voice notes and photos in; a voice note, a PDF and a live website back out.
A private answer to one member — the others see that it happened, not what it said.
We deleted the machine out from under the room; the next message brought it back.
